chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
A group of people entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and saw him dyed with black [henna/dye]. So they asked him, and he said: 'I am a man who loves women, and I adorn myself for them.'

key_terms.أَتَصَنَّعُ: I adorn myself / I beautify myself
key_terms.مُخْتَضِباً: dyed (specifically with henna or black dye)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imams wear black dye according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) is observed wearing black dye, a practice often associated with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Imams to distinguish themselves or enhance their appearance. He clarifies that his motivation was not merely ritualistic but rooted in *takhalluq* (good character) and *tashabbuh* (adornment) to please his wives, illustrating the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual dignity with marital affection. This highlights the permissibility and virtue of using natural dyes like henna and katam for beautification within the bounds of modesty and love.
